static_traits.name: Catherine
static_traits.medical_history: Without significant physical illness; never received psychotherapy; without similar problem history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, strong logic, highly cooperative, Positive attitude, able to engage in rational discussion and willing to try exercises; speech rate Not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I persistently fear that despite being very active in weightlifting and marathons, I will eventually be injured and unable to exercise anymore. This Fear has lasted months, bringing marked Anxiety and distress.
basic_info.core_demands: The fear of injury has begun to affect my motivation to take part in sports activities, so I am seeking professional support and guidance.
growth_experiences: Long engaged in weightlifting and marathons, no serious injuries for years; in recent months after a mild muscle strain in one weightlifting session, Fear markedly worsened.
Hearing multiple stories of Athletes having to stop exercising after injuries, these external narratives Reinforced her worry about uncontrollable future injuries.

core_beliefs: I will eventually get injured and lose athletic ability

special_situations.event: After a mild muscle strain occurred during a weightlifting session
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If any pain appears, it necessarily predicts more serious injury, eventually being unable to continue exercising
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pays more attention to movement standards and warm-ups, continuously monitors bodily sensations and reduces activity intensity for safety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This strain shows I am about to suffer serious injury, possibly never able to exercise again

special_situations.event: Hearing stories of Athletes having to stop exercising due to injuries
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others encounter serious injuries, my luck will also run out, sooner or later I will be injured and stop the same way
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently expresses worries during training, seeks comfort from peers and confirmation of safety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My luck will run out one day, and I will get injured and be forced to stop

special_situations.event: Every time he engages in physical activity (weightlifting or running)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as engaging in high-intensity activity, injury is almost unavoidable, any discomfort is a sign of injury
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Keeps high caution, adjusting or reducing load and intensity at any time to avoid potential injury
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may be injuring myself right now, once injured I cannot exercise again

special_situations.event: When reviewing own years of training experience, especially focusing on that mild strain while ignoring the large record of not yet being injured
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative events explain true risk better than positive experiences, safe experiences 'do not count'
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly recalls negative experiences, weakening or ignoring evidence of one's recovery and safety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Although not seriously injured for years, this strain is the key, showing I am not safe

core_conflict.wish: Longing to maintain physical vitality and safety, continuously participating in exercise Freely
core_conflict.fear: Fearing losing exercise ability and Independence, having life's focus taken away by uncontrollable injuries
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of security and reducing uncertainty through rational analysis and strict Self-monitoring

object_relations.self_representation: The injury-prone athlete needing constant vigilance
object_relations.object_representation: Training partners / others who may ignore risks or not understand own worries

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites him to do reality testing or discuss the evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understands the counseling situation as one where rational rules must be used to control risk, otherwise catastrophe will occur (toward others' suggestions, carries an implication of control and safety review)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes technical details and data in a calm, rational and well-organized tone, downplaying emotional expression; when fear is touched upon, turns the conversation to action norms and preventive measures.

manifestations: Worrying about being unable to continue exercising after injury, feeling 'sooner or later will lose exercise Freedom'
Rehearsing worst outcomes in every activity, Reinforcing Fear of physical limitations
outcomes: Relationship tension when exercising with friends

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Constantly emphasizing correct posture, warm-up, and 'listening to the body' in counseling and training, staying highly cautious about activities
Frequent self-checking and seeking safety reassurance

exception_events.target_problem: When doing high-intensity training or running, the client is typically trapped by Fear of injury, showing strong Anxiety and reduced participation motivation.
exception_events.unique_outcome: After that mild muscle strain, she did not completely stop activity or fall into panic, but chose to rest, followed the Recovery plan, and finally Recovered smoothly to normal.
exception_events.reason: Cues: taking different actions (following the Recovery plan, slowing pace, Listening to body feedback), thus this time not fully trapped by Fear and achieving Recovery.

positive_force: Years of sustained exercise experience and fitness foundation (long-term weightlifting and marathons without serious injury)
Having safety strategies: valuing correct form, warm-up, and Listening to the body
Positive attitude, willing to cooperate with reality testing and cognitive restructuring
negative_force: Cognitive distortions like catastrophizing, predicting the future, overgeneralization, and mental filtering
Persistent worry about injury causing Sleep affected and Decreased drive
Influenced by others' injury stories; external information intensifies fear

target_behavior.behavior: High Anxiety and Anticipatory worry appearing in exercise-related situations
antecedent: When doing weight training or running
Recalling or hearing stories of Athletes getting injured
After experiencing a mild muscle strain
Worrying about getting hurt before falling asleep
target_behavior.core_reason: Others' injury stories and the recent strain experience triggering catastrophic and future-predicting cognitions, worrying about losing exercise ability
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential danger; seeks safety and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased exercise motivation, Tense relationships with friends, Sleep affected and Overall happiness lowered
